summary: Ottawa hair stylist Adamo DiNardo, owner of Hair by Adamo & Co., walks David DiNardo through the business side of a career that started at age 14: opening a 700-square-foot salon on Preston Street after a phone call with his dad, packing 12 people into it within two and a half years, and signing a lease on a 3,000-square-foot space in the middle of the pandemic. He explains how he builds a culture of psychological safety with 17 staff, why he still works five days a week behind the chair, and how he is now carving out admin days to plan the next phase of growth.
takeaways: Adamo started in salons at 14 and opened Hair by Adamo & Co. in a 700-square-foot space on Preston Street after telling his dad he wanted something small; a space was offered within eight hours.
The first location grew to 12 people in 700 square feet in two and a half years before he knocked through to the unit next door and doubled the footprint.
COVID shutdowns hit salons three times because they were not deemed essential; curbside product pickup, delivered by volunteering stylists, kept the business afloat.
He signed the lease on a roughly 3,000-square-foot salon during the pandemic because capacity rules meant the old space could never bring back the same numbers.
His core value is a safe space where staff and clients can be their authentic selves, and his rule for conflict is 'come to me first' before problems simmer and boil over.
Adamo still cuts hair five days a week from 9 to 6 or 7, and says the hard part of business is fitting payroll, accounting and staff conversations around the craft he loves.
In the past five years every one of his teammates has bought a home, which he counts as proof the business is working; his sticky-note advice is 'keep going, don't look back, and smile'.
